chunks: Al-Husayn ibn 'Ubayd Allah informed me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from 'Imran ibn Musa, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from his father, from 'Abd al-Hamid ibn 'Awwad, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:
I heard him say: Whoever sleeps while he is in ruku', or in sajdah, or walking, in whichever of these states, then wudu (ablution) is obligatory upon him.

key_terms.الْوُضُوءُ: wudu (ablution), the ritual purification required for acts like salat
key_terms.رَاكِعٌ: one who is in ruku' (bowing in prayer)
key_terms.نَامَ: slept; entered a state of sleep

ai.seo_question: Does sleeping while bowing, prostrating, or walking invalidate wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling that sleep invalidates wudu (ablution), even if it occurs during bodily states such as ruku', sajdah, or walking. It is relevant to ritual purity and the rules governing readiness for salat (prayer).
